title: SAC Jets and Navy Shell Sanae Township, Kyaukphyu District — 100+ Homes Destroyed, 50,000+ Displaced as AA Advances on Chinese-Backed Port
detail: Myanmar junta forces conducting sustained aerial and naval bombardment of Sanae Township in Kyaukphyu District, Rakhine State — where the Arakan Army is actively advancing on Myanmar's most strategically sensitive port — according to CDM documentation for May 21, 2026. SAC aircraft bombed Shwe Hintha Ward in Sanae town, destroying at least 100 homes and forcing tens of thousands of civilians to flee from more than ten villages in the surrounding area. Naval vessel shelling by junta warships caused additional civilian casualties. The AA is simultaneously advancing on Kyaukphyu — the site of China's $7.3-billion deep-sea port project, natural gas pipeline terminal, and Special Economic Zone under the China-Myanmar Economic Corridor (CMEC). Heavy ground clashes are ongoing near Thaingchaung and Zaichaung villages approximately 10 miles south of Kyaukphyu town. The junta deployed jet fighters and Y-12 aircraft in multiple strike waves against AA positions and civilian areas in the Kyaukphyu-Sanae corridor. Earlier in May 2026, the AA repelled a junta amphibious assault from Taungmawgyi naval base, blocking landing craft attempting to reinforce Sanae town via the Thanzit River. AA forces report surrounding approximately 50,000 civilians displaced from the Sanae area face urgent humanitarian needs with roads cut. The Kyaukphyu offensive has major geopolitical implications: Chinese investments and personnel at the deep-sea port have prompted Beijing to signal concern, while China's protection of its CMEC interests was a factor in its recent diplomatic engagement with both the SAC (Wang Yi's April 2026 Naypyidaw visit) and resistance EAOs. The AA controls approximately 90% of Rakhine State and is the only major EAO whose operations directly threaten Chinese-flagged infrastructure in Myanmar.

media.caption: SAC aircraft and navy bombard Sanae, Kyaukphyu District — 100+ homes destroyed, 50,000+ displaced as AA advances on China-backed CMEC port — Irrawaddy, May 2026

title: TNLA Rejects China-Brokered Junta Demand to Surrender Four Northern Shan State Towns — Kunming Talks (May 12-13) Fail to Produce Agreement
detail: The Palaung State Liberation Front/Ta'ang National Liberation Army (PSLF/TNLA) has rejected a Myanmar junta demand brokered at China-mediated talks in Kunming (May 12-13, 2026) that TNLA surrender four towns in northern Shan State: Namhkam, Namtu, Mongngawt, and Monglon — located 67 to 214 kilometers north and west of Lashio, captured from SAC control during and after Operation 1027 (October 2023). The junta, backed by Chinese diplomatic support, demanded TNLA cede the four towns as a precondition for political recognition of TNLA's governance in Ta'ang areas captured since 2023. TNLA rejected the demand, maintaining its position from the October 2025 China-brokered partial ceasefire under which TNLA had already yielded Momeik Township in Shan State and Mogok Township in Mandalay Region as concessions to Chinese pressure, while the junta separately recaptured Hsipaw, Kyaukme, and Nawnghkio townships. The failed Kunming talks reveal the limits of Chinese diplomatic coercion over TNLA: while China retains significant leverage over the traditionally China-aligned TNLA and MNDAA through border trade and historical relationships, TNLA's leadership views the Namhkam-Namtu corridor as a core strategic interest linked to Ta'ang ethnic governance and will not yield it even under Chinese pressure. The TNLA's April 15, 2026 political statement welcoming Min Aung Hlaing's government — which analysts attributed to Chinese pressure — thus has not translated into territorial concessions. The NUG and KIO have not commented publicly on the talks. China's position is complicated by its simultaneous diplomatic backing of the SAC (Wang Yi's April Naypyidaw visit) and its historical ties to TNLA/MNDAA, reflecting Beijing's ultimately self-interested strategic calculation around CMEC investments and border stability rather than principled mediation.

media.caption: TNLA rejects China-brokered junta demand to surrender four northern Shan State towns; Kunming talks fail — Border Lens analysis, May 20, 2026
